primary_sources: Robert H. Clancy, Congressional Record, 68th Congress, 1st Session, 1924

stimulus.text: Paraphrase of Representative Robert H. Clancy, speaking in the House of Representatives in 1924 against the immigration bill: Clancy said that newcomers had always faced bitter complaints, from the Irish and Germans of the 1840s to the Italians, Poles, Jews, Greeks, and Russians of his own day. He called the bill's use of the 1890 census “racial discrimination at its worst,” a deliberate attempt to aim a blow at the peoples of eastern and southern Europe.
stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of Robert H. Clancy, Congressional Record, 68th Congress, 1st Session, 1924 (public domain, U.S. government). The quoted phrase “racial discrimination at its worst” is Clancy's own wording.

source: original; stimulus paraphrased from Robert H. Clancy, Congressional Record, 1924, public domain
stem: The policy Clancy opposed most directly led to which later result?

options.text: a long pause in mass immigration for forty years
a sharp rise in immigration from Asia instead
options.misconception: The 1924 act barred immigration from Asia. Asian immigration fell to almost nothing, it did not rise.

options.text: the repeal of all immigration laws in 1930
options.misconception: No repeal came in 1930. The quota system stayed in place until the Immigration Act of 1965.

options.text: open borders with Europe in the years after 1924
options.misconception: The act did the opposite of opening borders. It capped total immigration at 150,000 a year and favored a few groups.

rationales.A: Background from the books: the quota acts cut immigration so deeply that mass immigration paused for over forty years, until the Immigration Act of 1965 ended the national-origins quotas.
rationales.B: The 1924 act barred immigration from Asia. Asian immigration fell to almost nothing, it did not rise.
rationales.C: No repeal came in 1930. The quota system stayed in place until the Immigration Act of 1965.
rationales.D: The act did the opposite of opening borders. It capped total immigration at 150,000 a year and favored a few groups.
rationales.general:
1. Name the policy Clancy fought: the national-origins quotas of 1924.
2. Ask what the quotas did: they cut the flow from southern and eastern Europe and barred Asia.
3. Ask how long the cut lasted. Background: the quota system stayed until the Immigration Act of 1965 ended it.
4. Name the result: a pause in mass immigration of about forty years.
Remember: a law's effect is measured over its whole life, not only the year it passed.
